content: 1. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Close monitoring is recommended when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Chloramphenicol decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Close monitoring is recommended. 4. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 7. Clindamycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 9. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 10. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. Close monitoring is recommended. 11. Colesevelam decreases the levels of norethindrone by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Oral contraceptives containing norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol should be administered at least 4 hours before colesevelam to avoid decreased absorption. 12. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 13. Crofelemer increases the levels of norethindrone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Crofelemer has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 in the gut but is unlikely to have systemic effects due to minimal absorption. Close monitoring is recommended. 14. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone by inhibiting their metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 15. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of cyclosporine by an unknown mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. 16. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. 17. Danazol increases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting their metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 18. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP substrates. Dose reduction of BCRP substrates should be considered based on prescribing information. Close monitoring is recommended. 19. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 20. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Close monitoring is recommended. 21. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Close monitoring is recommended. 22. Demeclocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Ethinyl estradiol may decrease the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), leading to increased serum concentrations and potential adverse effects. Close monitoring is recommended. 24. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 25. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of diazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. Close monitoring is recommended. 26. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting their metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 29. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 30. Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. 31. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for at least 1 week after discontinuation. 32. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the efficacy of elagolix by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce elagolix efficacy. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 33. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. Close monitoring is recommended. 34. Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by an unknown mechanism. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 35. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. Co-administration should be avoided due to the risk of serious toxicities. 36. Encorafenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after the last dose. 37. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the efficacy of enoxaparin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 38. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 39. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 40. Erythromycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised.
